concepts.name: Tundra
concepts.definition: Cold, treeless biome where frigid temperatures, short growing seasons and permafrost limit vegetation to shrubs, sedges, mosses and lichens; the WWF biome covers the polar tundra, while alpine tundra on mountaintops is classed separately.

concepts.name: Taiga
concepts.alt_names: boreal forest, snow forest (WWF: boreal forests/taiga)
concepts.definition: The world's largest land biome, a belt of coniferous forest (pine, spruce, larch) spanning high northern latitudes across Canada, Alaska, Scandinavia and Russia.

concepts.name: Temperate broadleaf and mixed forest
concepts.alt_names: temperate deciduous forest is its core (WWF: temperate broadleaf and mixed forests)
concepts.definition: Temperate biome of broadleaf, mixed broadleaf-conifer and temperate rainforest, in regions with moderate temperatures and adequate rainfall, notably eastern North America, Europe and central China. Broader than 'temperate deciduous forest': it also covers mixed conifer stands and the Southern Hemisphere's evergreen Nothofagus and eucalypt forests.

concepts.name: Temperate coniferous forest
concepts.alt_names: includes temperate rainforest (WWF: temperate conifer forests)
concepts.definition: Temperate biome dominated by conifers such as pine, fir and redwood, occurring in mild rainy coastal zones and inland mountains across North America, Eurasia and Australasia; it takes in temperate rainforest, not just uniform pine and spruce stands.

concepts.name: Tropical moist forest
concepts.alt_names: tropical rainforest is its core (WWF: tropical and subtropical moist broadleaf forests)
concepts.definition: Tropical and subtropical biome of evergreen to semi-deciduous broadleaf forest with high rainfall, exemplified by the Amazon, Congo and Indo-Malayan forests. Wider than 'rainforest' alone: monsoon forest, montane cloud forest and freshwater swamp forest are all inside it.

concepts.name: Tropical dry forest
concepts.alt_names: monsoon forest (WWF: tropical and subtropical dry broadleaf forests)
concepts.definition: Warm tropical and subtropical biome of largely deciduous forest with long dry seasons, best developed in western Mexico, the Bolivian lowlands and parts of Africa and South Asia.

concepts.name: Temperate grassland and shrubland
concepts.alt_names: prairie, steppe, pampas, veld (WWF: temperate grasslands, savannas and shrublands)
concepts.definition: Temperate biome dominated by grasses and shrubs, including prairies, steppes and pampas across North America, Eurasia, South America and southern Africa; tree-scattered savanna and shrubland belong to it too, not only open grass.

concepts.name: Tropical grassland and savanna
concepts.alt_names: savanna, cerrado, llanos (WWF: tropical and subtropical grasslands, savannas and shrublands)
concepts.definition: Tropical and subtropical biome of grass- and shrub-dominated country in semi-arid to semi-humid climates, widespread across Africa, South and Southeast Asia, South America and Australia; the tree-grass savanna mosaic is its centre, but pure grassland and shrubland count as well.

concepts.name: Mediterranean woodland and scrub
concepts.alt_names: chaparral, maquis, fynbos, matorral (WWF: Mediterranean forests, woodlands and scrub)
concepts.definition: Biome of the Mediterranean climate's dry summers and wet winters, found in the Mediterranean Basin, California, central Chile, South Africa's Cape and southern Australia; sclerophyll woodland and oak and pine forest belong to it alongside the scrub.

concepts.name: Desert and xeric shrubland
concepts.alt_names: desert scrub (WWF: deserts and xeric shrublands)
concepts.definition: Arid biome receiving under about 250 mm of rain yearly, covering roughly a fifth of Earth's land with drought-adapted shrubs and sparse vegetation across every continent.

concepts.name: Mangrove
concepts.definition: Coastal biome of salt-tolerant shrubs and trees growing in tropical and subtropical intertidal zones, mostly between 30 degrees north and south latitude.
